summary: San Diego International Airport (SAN), originally Lindbergh Field, sits about 3 miles northwest of downtown San Diego and is known for its close-in, bayfront location. It operates one main commercial runway, making it one of the busiest single-runway airports in the United States. Its compact layout and downtown proximity give travelers quick access to the city, harbor, and Balboa Park.
faqs:
Q: How far is San Diego International Airport from downtown?
A: It is roughly 3 miles (5 km) northwest of downtown San Diego, typically a 10–15 minute drive depending on traffic.

Q: How many terminals does SAN have?
A: SAN has Terminal 1 and Terminal 2, with airlines split between them; check your carrier before heading to the airport.

Q: Is San Diego International Airport a single-runway airport?
A: Yes, its commercial operations use one main runway, which contributes to its reputation as one of the busiest single-runway airports in the U.S.

Q: What is the best way to get to downtown San Diego from SAN?
A: Taxis, rideshares, and public buses are available; the Metropolitan Transit System Route 992 connects the airport area with downtown and is a budget-friendly option.
transport_tips: Rideshare pickup zones are marked outside each terminal; follow signs rather than accepting unsolicited rides. The MTS Route 992 bus offers a cheap connection to downtown and Santa Fe Depot, while taxis and shuttles are readily available. Because the airport is so close to downtown, traffic on Harbor Drive and I-5 can be heavy during commute hours, so allow extra time.
local_tip: Frequent visitors know that if you're landing westbound on Runway 27, the left side of the plane offers a close-up view of downtown San Diego as you approach.
